problem: Beam-search reranking in seq2seq VLN scores each trajectory by averaging locally normalized per-step action scores, which are incomparable across different trajectories and so bias the ranking (label bias).
motivation: Beam search at inference gives strong VLN performance, but the trajectory-level ranking depends on biased local scores. Rescaling scores at the trajectory level should give more comparable scores and better final trajectory selection.
key_idea: Replace locally normalized average-of-step scores with beam-constrained global normalization, using two global score functions to rerank all candidate trajectories in the output beam.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract's claim is that the bias comes from local discriminative classifiers producing incomparable unit scores, and that global rescaling over the beam alleviates it.
method: Beam-constrained global normalization: rescales trajectory-level scores over the candidates in the output beam rather than using local per-step normalization
Two global score functions: used to rerank all candidate trajectories in the beam, giving more comparable trajectory scores
Seq2seq VLN baseline with beam-search decoding: the underlying agent whose candidate trajectories are reranked
